current.text: Jaylen Brown is gone. Jayson Tatum, back for a full season, and Paul George effectively replace him. Mitchell Robinson was also added.
Experts expect Boston to be a better and deeper regular season team than last season.
One expert does not think the new roster improves Boston's title chances.
Karalis predicts 48 wins. He says the East is tougher and there will be fewer tanking teams to beat.
Paul George is clearly the number two option behind Jayson Tatum.
Payton Pritchard's usage path is more crowded than last season. Tatum, George and Derrick White are ahead of him, so Brown's exit gives him no extra opportunity.

The starting five is not settled. The depth chart has Pritchard and Queta starting. The newest expert projection has White, Baylor Scheierman, Tatum, George and Neemias Queta starting, with Pritchard, Sam Hauser, Robinson, Jordan Walsh and Mike Conley off the bench.
The starting center is still open between Queta and Robinson. An earlier projection had Robinson and Hauser starting.
The team is very deep, with at least 12 rotation-level players. In a 10-man rotation, Walsh or another player will sit most nights. Ron Harper Jr. is outside the rotation.
The supporting cast has clearer roles than last season, which should make it easier to fit in George and Robinson.
Boston has 14 players on the roster and one open two-way slot.
Three-point volume should stay high, but with less five-out. The plan is four shooters around a big in the dunker spot. Tatum will play only some small-ball center.
Boston has 16 back-to-backs, tied with Brooklyn for the most in the league.
The many back-to-backs mainly hurt Paul George and Mitchell Robinson, the players most likely to rest.
The playoff schedule is 4-3-4 games through March 28, one game short of the maximum. It includes three back-to-backs in the playoff window.

durable.text: Boston gets a lot out of players with limited offense, such as Jordan Walsh.

note: Tatum and Paul George take over Jaylen Brown's usage as the clear one-two. This squeezes Payton Pritchard and gives little extra to White and the other role players on a very deep, winning team. The most back-to-backs in the league (16) adds rest risk for George and Mitchell Robinson, though the playoff weeks still have 11 games. Watch early who starts on the wing (Scheierman, Pritchard or Hauser) and at center (Queta or Robinson).
